title: movement_indicator_none_test's placeholder check is now vacuous (matches the testid, not the glyph)
evidence:
client_test.gleam:1780-1782 (updated by this diff):
  html |> string.contains("data-testid=\"movement-none\"") |> should.be_true
  html |> string.contains("aria-label=\"No change\"") |> should.be_true
  html |> string.contains("-") |> should.be_true

The rendered element (movement_indicator.gleam:33-42) carries a hyphen in its testid:
    "none" ->
      html.span(
        [
          attribute("data-testid", "movement-none"),
          attribute("aria-label", "No change"),
          class("text-slate text-sm"),
        ],
        [html.text("-")],
      )

The previous assertion used the em-dash ("\u{2014}"), which does not occur in the testid/class; the replacement "-" also occurs in `movement-none`, so contains("-") is satisfied by the testid alone.
detail: After swapping the em-dash for a hyphen, contains("-") is satisfied by the `movement-none` testid, not the placeholder text node; removing html.text("-") would still pass the test.
recommended_fix: Assert the text node directly, e.g. the rendered `>-<` boundary, or a glyph that does not collide with the testid, so the placeholder render stays pinned.
